Stability of the Courtade–Kumar inequalityThanks: Tuan Tran was supported by the Excellent Young Talents Program (Overseas) of the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant No. GG0010007003.

Vu Khac Ky Address: Department of Mathematics, FPT University, Hanoi, Vietnam Email address: kyvk2@fpt.edu.vn and Tuan Tran Address: School of Mathematical Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China, Anhui, China Email address: trantuan@ustc.edu.cn
Abstract.

We prove dimension-independent stability for the Courtade–Kumar inequality: a Boolean function f:{−1,1}n→{−1,1}f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\} whose information is close to the dictator value is close in probability to a signed dictator. The correlation dependence is sharp in order near zero and, for increasing functions, also at the noiseless endpoint.

1. Introduction

How much information can a one-bit summary of independent fair bits carry about a noisy observation of those bits? The Courtade–Kumar conjecture [2], a longstanding problem in information theory, asserted that keeping one input bit is optimal. We study the corresponding stability question: if a summary retains nearly as much information, how often can it differ from one of the original bits or its complement? Our bounds are independent of the number of input bits.

To formulate the question, let XX be uniform on {−1,1}n\{-1,1\}^{n}, where n≥1n\geq 1. For 0≤ρ≤10\leq\rho\leq 1, its noisy observation Yρ∈{−1,1}nY_{\rho}\in\{-1,1\}^{n} is obtained by flipping each coordinate of XX independently with probability (1−ρ)/2(1-\rho)/2. A one-bit summary is f⁡(X)f(X), where f:{−1,1}n→{−1,1}f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\} is Boolean. Keeping one coordinate, possibly changing its sign, corresponds to a signed dictator σ​Xi\sigma X_{i}, with 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n and σ∈{−1,1}\sigma\in\{-1,1\}. We call ff increasing if f⁡(x)≤f⁡(y)f(x)\leq f(y) whenever xi≤yix_{i}\leq y_{i} for every ii. It is balanced if its two values are equally likely under the uniform input.

We measure uncertainty by binary Shannon entropy, Hb​(p)=−p​log⁡p−(1−p)​log⁡(1−p)H_{\rm b}(p)=-p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p) for a Bernoulli bit with success probability p∈[0,1]p\in[0,1]. All logarithms are natural, and 0​log⁡0=00\log 0=0. For a {−1,1}\{-1,1\}-valued bit with mean t∈[−1,1]t\in[-1,1], we write H⁡(t)=Hb​((1−t)/2)H(t)=H_{\rm b}((1-t)/2) for its entropy and Φ⁡(t)=log⁡2−H⁡(t)\Phi(t)=\log 2-H(t) for its entropy deficit relative to a fair bit. The latter is also the relative entropy of its law with respect to the uniform law on {−1,1}\{-1,1\}. Both HH and Φ\Phi take values in [0,log⁡2][0,\log 2].

The mutual information I⁡(f⁡(X),Yρ)I(f(X);Y_{\rho}) measures the reduction in this uncertainty: it is the entropy of f⁡(X)f(X) minus its conditional entropy given YρY_{\rho}. For a signed dictator these entropies are log⁡2\log 2 and H⁡(ρ)H(\rho), respectively, so its information is Φ⁡(ρ)\Phi(\rho).

The optimality of this value was conjectured by Courtade and Kumar [2] and proved independently in our companion paper, Dictators are most informative [8], and in [1]. We refer to our companion paper for detailed background and prior work.

Theorem ([8, 1]).

For every Boolean function f:{−1,1}n→{−1,1}f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\} and every 0≤ρ≤10\leq\rho\leq 1, with X,YρX,Y_{\rho} as above,

I⁡(f⁡(X),Yρ)≤I⁡(X1,Yρ)=Φ⁡(ρ).I(f(X);Y_{\rho})\leq I(X_{1};Y_{\rho})=\Phi(\rho).

The following stability theorem, announced in our companion paper [8], is the main result of this work. Its proof develops an entropy-barrier approach, together with quantitative estimates that track the information deficit and the effect of compression. We use analytic tools from the companion paper, but do not assume the Courtade–Kumar inequality.

Theorem 1.1 (Stability).

Let 0<ρ<10<\rho<1 and ε≥0\varepsilon\geq 0. If a Boolean function f:{−1,1}n→{−1,1}f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\} satisfies I⁡(f⁡(X),Yρ)≥Φ⁡(ρ)−εI(f(X);Y_{\rho})\geq\Phi(\rho)-\varepsilon, then there are 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n and σ∈{−1,1}\sigma\in\{-1,1\} such that

ℙ⁡(f⁡(X)≠σ​Xi)≤108​ερ2​(1−ρ)​H​(ρ).\mathbb{P}\left(f(X)\neq\sigma X_{i}\right)\leq\frac{10^{8}\varepsilon}{\rho^{2}(1-\rho)H(\rho)}.

If ff is increasing, one can choose ii so that

ℙ⁡(f⁡(X)≠Xi)≤108​ερ2​H​(ρ).\mathbb{P}\left(f(X)\neq X_{i}\right)\leq\frac{10^{8}\varepsilon}{\rho^{2}H(\rho)}.

Taking ε=0\varepsilon=0 shows that equality in the Courtade–Kumar bound holds precisely for signed dictators when 0<ρ<10<\rho<1. The endpoint dependence is intrinsic: at ρ=1\rho=1, every balanced Boolean function carries log⁡2\log 2 information, including functions far from dictators.

Three-variable majority shows that both bounds have optimal order as ρ↓0\rho\downarrow 0, and that the increasing-function bound also has optimal order as ρ↑1\rho\uparrow 1 (Section 5.6).

1.1. Method and contributions

Stability requires more than ruling out a violation of the Courtade–Kumar inequality: the information deficit must control the distance to a dictator. We use entropy production to follow the decrease of conditional entropy as correlation increases. The key additional requirement is a quantitative surplus over the dictator’s production rate even when the conditional entropy exceeds H⁡(ρ)H(\rho), with a controlled loss depending on the information deficit. This larger entropy changes the profile heights used in the production estimates, but a single dilation factor controls all the changes: one plus the positive information deficit divided by H⁡(ρ)H(\rho). Two energy comparisons hold under an arbitrary entropy budget: the spectral estimate uses Fourier energy, while the marked-coordinate estimate separates a dominant coordinate from the remaining variance. Converting these comparisons to stability loses only a term linear in the deficit.

We combine these estimates by comparing the deficit with a constant multiple of H⁡(ρ)H(\rho) times the distance to a nearest signed dictator. If it fell below this curve, the production surplus would force the difference to keep decreasing as correlation approaches one. This contradicts the nonnegative deficit Φ⁡(𝔼​f)\Phi(\mathbb{E}f) at the noiseless endpoint. The comparison in Section 3 works pointwise in correlation, so a source may move between the local and spectral regions. Quantitative compression then transfers stability from increasing to arbitrary functions by accounting for the information gained during sorting.

At lower correlations we use the local and Fourier estimates of Samorodnitsky [5] and Yu [6, 7], in the forms established in [8], together with its strict profile-clock comparisons. All inputs are stated explicitly. The parameter checks are collected in the appendices, and the constants are chosen for convenience. The verification repository is https://github.com/vukhacky/CK-stability; Appendix B describes the certificates and replay procedure.

3. From entropy estimates to stability

Three principles organize the stability proof. A production criterion compares the deficit with a multiple of H⁡(ρ)H(\rho). Profile dilation keeps that deficit in every coordinate estimate. Quantitative compression then controls the distance lost when passing to an increasing function.

3.1. Comparison with an entropy barrier

Write ρ=tanh⁡u\rho=\tanh u and measure the deficit relative to the dictator’s remaining uncertainty:

(3.1) Zf​(u)=Δtanh⁡u​(f)H⁡(tanh⁡u).Z_{f}(u)=\frac{\Delta_{\tanh u}(f)}{H(\tanh u)}.

Write s+=max⁡{s,0}s_{+}=\max\{s,0\} for the positive part of a real number. In the criterion below, aa measures the production surplus and BB its loss per unit of normalized deficit. The production estimate is needed only below the threshold Zf​(u)<η​δ​(f)Z_{f}(u)<\eta\delta(f); above it, the desired lower bound already holds. The proof compares Δρ​(f)\Delta_{\rho}(f) with the barrier c​H​(ρ)​δ​(f)cH(\rho)\delta(f) using the endpoint identity (2.3).

Both production estimates below have this form: spectral transfer supplies the surplus away from dictators, and a marked coordinate supplies it near them. The criterion allows these estimates to alternate with a direct local bound; no single region must persist as correlation increases.

3.3. Quantitative compression

The classical compression reduction of Courtade and Kumar [2, Lemma 2] shows that sorting coordinate fibers increasingly does not decrease mutual information. For a Boolean function ff, sorting once in each coordinate produces an increasing Boolean function gg satisfying

𝔼g=𝔼f,Aρ(g)≥Aρ(f),δ(g)≤δ(f)(0<ρ<1).\mathbb{E}g=\mathbb{E}f,\qquad A_{\rho}(g)\geq A_{\rho}(f),\qquad\delta(g)\leq\delta(f)\qquad(0<\rho<1).

See [8, Lemma 2.1] for this formulation, including the comparison of dictator distances. These comparisons reduce information maximization to increasing functions, but do not by themselves transfer stability: a bound on δ⁡(g)\delta(g) need not control δ⁡(f)\delta(f). The next lemma supplies the missing quantitative estimate, controlling the original dictator distance by the compressed distance and the information gained during sorting.

Lemma 3.3.

Let gg be obtained from f:{−1,1}n→{−1,1}f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\} by sorting each coordinate increasingly, once per coordinate. For 0<ρ<10<\rho<1,

ρ2​(1−ρ2)​δ​(f)≤Aρ​(g)−Aρ​(f)+ρ2​(2−ρ2)​δ​(g).\rho^{2}(1-\rho^{2})\delta(f)\leq A_{\rho}(g)-A_{\rho}(f)+\rho^{2}(2-\rho^{2})\delta(g).

Δρ​(f)≥ρ2​(1−ρ2)​min⁡{1,cρ2​(2−ρ2)}​δ​(f).\Delta_{\rho}(f)\geq\rho^{2}(1-\rho^{2})\min\left\{1,\frac{c}{\rho^{2}(2-\rho^{2})}\right\}\delta(f).

Choose ii with g^​(i)=1−2​δ​(g)\widehat{g}(i)=1-2\delta(g). Immediately before coordinate ii is sorted, write the current source as b+xi​db+x_{i}d. Sorting any other coordinate preserves the iith singleton coefficient. Thus 𝔼​d=f^​(i)\mathbb{E}d=\widehat{f}(i) and 𝔼​|d|=g^​(i)\mathbb{E}|d|=\widehat{g}(i). Also d∈{−1,0,1}d\in\{-1,0,1\}, so 𝔼​d2=g^​(i)\mathbb{E}d^{2}=\widehat{g}(i).

At each noisy output of the other coordinates, the function v↦[Φ⁡(Tρ​b+ρ​v)+Φ⁡(Tρ​b−ρ​v)]/2v\mapsto[\Phi(T_{\rho}b+\rho v)+\Phi(T_{\rho}b-\rho v)]/2 is even and has second derivative at least ρ2\rho^{2} on its feasible interval. Now 1−f^​(i)2≥2​δ​(f)1-\widehat{f}(i)^{2}\geq 2\delta(f), 1−g^​(i)=2​δ​(g)1-\widehat{g}(i)=2\delta(g), and 1+g^​(i)−ρ2≤2−ρ21+\widehat{g}(i)-\rho^{2}\leq 2-\rho^{2}. Substituting these bounds and adding the nonnegative gains from all other sorting steps proves the first assertion.

4. Local and intermediate correlations

We first describe the deficit when ff approaches a dictator at a fixed correlation. A relative-entropy calculation gives the leading term and an explicit remainder for arbitrary mean. In the balanced case, the leading coefficient agrees with Yu’s asymptotic bound [7, Theorem 4.2].

Corollary 4.1 (Local stability).

Let f:{−1,1}n→{−1,1}f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\} and 0<ρ<10<\rho<1, and put δ=δ⁡(f)\delta=\delta(f) and μ=𝔼​f\mu=\mathbb{E}f. Then

0≤Aρ​(f)−Φ⁡(ρ)+2​ρ​atanh⁡(ρ)​δ+Φ⁡(μ)≤4​δ2/(1+ρ2)1−ρ2.0\leq A_{\rho}(f)-\Phi(\rho)+2\rho\atanh(\rho)\delta+\Phi(\mu)\leq\frac{4\delta^{2/(1+\rho^{2})}}{1-\rho^{2}}.

Orient a closest dictator as xix_{i} and write g=Tρ​fg=T_{\rho}f. For s∈[−1,1]s\in[-1,1] and t∈(−1,1)t\in(-1,1), the expression Φ⁡(s)−Φ⁡(t)−atanh⁡(t)​(s−t)\Phi(s)-\Phi(t)-\atanh(t)(s-t) is the relative entropy between Bernoulli laws of means ss and tt. It lies between zero and (s−t)2/(1−t2)(s-t)^{2}/(1-t^{2}): the upper bound follows from log⁡x≤x−1\log x\leq x-1. Average with s=g⁡(X)s=g(X) and t=ρ​Xit=\rho X_{i}. Hypercontractivity [8, Theorem 3.1] gives ‖Tρ​(f−xi)‖22≤‖f−xi‖1+ρ22=4​δ2/(1+ρ2)\|T_{\rho}(f-x_{i})\|_{2}^{2}\leq\|f-x_{i}\|_{1+\rho^{2}}^{2}=4\delta^{2/(1+\rho^{2})}, proving the upper bound. ∎

Since |μ|≤2​δ|\mu|\leq 2\delta and Φ⁡(μ)≤(log⁡2)​μ2\Phi(\mu)\leq(\log 2)\mu^{2}, the information deficit is 2​ρ​atanh⁡(ρ)​δ+Oρ​(δ2/(1+ρ2))2\rho\atanh(\rho)\delta+O_{\rho}(\delta^{2/(1+\rho^{2})}) as δ↓0\delta\downarrow 0, uniformly in the dimension. In particular, the leading coefficient is sharp, and the deficit is at least ρ​atanh⁡(ρ)​δ\rho\atanh(\rho)\delta for sufficiently small δ\delta at fixed ρ\rho. This local expansion assumes neither balance nor monotonicity.

5. Production bounds near the noiseless endpoint

We now establish the production estimates used in the entropy-barrier argument. A spectral comparison handles functions far from dictators; near a dictator, a marked-coordinate comparison preserves its profile and uses the variance in the remaining coordinates. Both estimates use the same entropy budget, and together they yield the stability bound at the end of this section. Throughout this section, let u>0u>0 and write ρ=tanh⁡u\rho=\tanh u and g=Tρ​fg=T_{\rho}f.

5.1. The spectral energy bound and its scalar cost

The quadratic bound in (2.4) leads to a nonnegative remainder Ψ\Psi and a useful variance identity:

(5.1) Ψ(t)=(log2)t2−Φ(t),𝒥=𝔼Ψ(g),(log⁡2)​Var⁡(g)=Φ⁡(ρ)−Δρ​(f)−Ψ⁡(μ)+𝒥.\begin{gathered}\Psi(t)=(\log 2)t^{2}-\Phi(t),\qquad\mathcal{J}=\mathbb{E}\Psi(g),\\ (\log 2)\Var(g)=\Phi(\rho)-\Delta_{\rho}(f)-\Psi(\mu)+\mathcal{J}.\end{gathered}

The entropy series gives 0≤Ψ⁡(t)≤(log⁡2−1/2)​t20\leq\Psi(t)\leq(\log 2-1/2)t^{2}. Also Ψ⁡(t)=H⁡(t)−(1−t2)​log⁡2≤H⁡(t)\Psi(t)=H(t)-(1-t^{2})\log 2\leq H(t). The marked-coordinate comparison will use 𝒥≥0\mathcal{J}\geq 0 to bound the variance from below. The spectral comparison retains this remainder: the scalar estimate in [8, Lemma 6.1] gives ‖arcsin⁡g−(π/2)​g‖22≤C∗​𝒥\|\arcsin g-(\pi/2)g\|_{2}^{2}\leq C_{*}\mathcal{J}, where C∗=(π/2−1)2/(log⁡2−1/2)C_{*}=(\pi/2-1)^{2}/(\log 2-1/2). Thus 𝒥\mathcal{J} controls the error in the linear approximation to the arcsine transform. Define ψ⁡(0)=0\psi(0)=0 and

(5.2) ψ⁡(a)=min⁡{a+a22,2​a​(1−a/4)log⁡(4/a)}for ​0<a≤1.\psi(a)=\min\left\{\frac{a+a^{2}}{2},\frac{2a(1-a/4)}{\log(4/a)}\right\}\quad\text{for }0<a\leq 1.

The retained-source estimate is Var⁡(PK​f)≤∑i∈Kψ⁡(f^​(i))\Var(P_{K}f)\leq\sum_{i\in K}\psi(\widehat{f}(i)) for increasing ff [8, Theorem 7.1].

The parameter tt sets the Fourier weights, while γ\gamma penalizes the error in replacing arcsin⁡g\arcsin g by (π/2)​g(\pi/2)g. Choose t≥2t\geq 2 and γ>max⁡{0,e2​t−3/2−t}\gamma>\max\{0,e^{2t-3}/2-t\}, and define

(5.3) k(s)=γ​sγ+s(s>−γ),Λ=π24k(t),Γ=γC∗,Δ2=[k(t)−k(2)]ρ4,Δ1=[k(t)−k(1)]ρ2,Δo=[k(t)−k(t−e2​t−3/2)]ρ2.\begin{gathered}k(s)=\frac{\gamma s}{\gamma+s}\ (s>-\gamma),\qquad\Lambda=\frac{\pi^{2}}{4}k(t),\qquad\Gamma=\gamma C_{*},\\ \Delta_{2}=[k(t)-k(2)]\rho^{4},\quad\Delta_{1}=[k(t)-k(1)]\rho^{2},\quad\Delta_{o}=[k(t)-k(t-e^{2t-3}/2)]\rho^{2}.\end{gathered}

The three costs Δ2,Δ1,Δo\Delta_{2},\Delta_{1},\Delta_{o} are nonnegative, with Δ1≥Δ2\Delta_{1}\geq\Delta_{2}. The next estimate separates the spectral baseline from the costs of retaining or discarding coordinates. We include the Fourier calculation from [8, Section 7.3, Lemma 7.4 and Proposition 7.5] to identify these costs before applying the profile budget.

Lemma 5.1 (Spectral energy).

Let f:{−1,1}n→{−1,1}f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\} be an increasing nonconstant Boolean function, and let K⊆[n]K\subseteq[n]. Then

Appendix B Certificates and reproducibility

The checks certify strict scalar inequalities and coverage of their domains. Low-correlation signs use rational series bounds; other transcendental signs use outward-rounded Arb intervals enclosing the exact values. A sign passes only when its whole enclosure has that sign. Exact rational and algebraic arithmetic checks coverage, and subdivisions retain both children unless infeasibility is proved. Convexity justifies the supporting lines; their integrals require positive denominators and the stated final signs. The compact inverse profile is bounded analytically, and separate scripts check the finite constants in Section 5.

B.4. The compact certificate

The file compact_uniform_certificate.json covers [45951/20000,8][45951/20000,8] by 24 closed rational intervals in uu: eight intervals through 44, followed by 16 intervals of length 1/41/4. Since 45951/20000<atanh⁡(49/50)45951/20000<\atanh(49/50), these intervals, together with the stated influence cutoffs, cover the full compact range required in Lemma 5.3.

The verifier compact_uniform_verify.py checks the four height inequalities per interval at 256 bits, using fourth-order Taylor enclosures. The independent audit compact_uniform_audit.py uses separately derived unscaled formulas and 384-bit arithmetic over the full extended height domain. Exact adjacency checks verify the partition, and check_stability_constants.py extracts the stability margins.

B.5. Files and replay scope

The repository for the certificates, verification code, and input data is https://github.com/vukhacky/CK-stability. The repository’s README.md gives installation instructions; python3 verify.py checks the manifest and replays all twelve numerical stages. Assertions must remain enabled. No file from the companion package is required.
